To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD can be used as a powerful tool in copolymerization studies.

1. the CD spectrum of a copolymer is the superposition of the contributions of the individual monomeric units; 2. the CD spectrum is a fingerprint of the monomer sequence distribution in copolymer chains; 3. the CD spectrum reflects conformational changes induced by solvents, temperature, pH; 4. the CD spectrum can be used to determine the absolute configuration of a chiral comonomer.

(i) copolymerization of a monomer with chiral side chain with a non chiroptical comonomer gives rise to a copolymer with induced optical activity; (ii) copolymer composition and sequence distribution can be obtained by CD analysis of copolymer in solution; (iii) CD analysis of copolymers in solution can provide information on the conformational state of the copolymer chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of optically active polymers and copolymers and with the study of their conformational behavior.
the synthesis of optically active polymers and copolymers, and their structural analysis by CD.

the following aspects: 1) synthesis of new monomers and their copolymers with chiral comonomers; 2) study of the conformational properties of the copolymers in solution and in the solid state; 3) study of the effect of chiral comonomer on the polymerization mechanism; 4) synthesis and characterization of copolymeric products with functional groups of interest for applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD spectroscopy is a powerful and versatile tool in the study of optically active and optically induced polymers.
CD can provide information on the structure, conformation, and configuration of copolymeric materials.
the study of the induced CD spectra of copolymers is a very useful and powerful technique to investigate copolymers structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that CD is a powerful and simple technique for the characterization of the structure of optically active polymers, copolymers and their solutions.
we have shown that CD is an extremely powerful technique for the analysis of optically inactive copolymers and for the characterization of the conformation of optically active ones.
CD spectroscopy is a very useful technique for the characterization and structural analysis of copolymers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD spectrum of a given copolymer can be predicted from the spectra of the two homopolymer constituents and from the copolymer composition.
CD is a useful tool for the characterization of copolymers, both in solution and in the solid state.
CD is a powerful tool for the analysis of copolymer structures and for studying their conformational features in solution.
